tools.name: add_to_workspace
tools.description: Add a company (or a note) to the shared on-page workspace the user is watching. Use it to build the target list as you research; the user can edit every row.

subtitle.description: One-line context, e.g. industry and size

reason.description: Why it belongs on the list

tools.name: build_campaign_brief
tools.description: Assemble an outbound feasibility brief: addressable market (live count when available), channel model math, matched case studies. The self-scoped pre-sales brief, computed instead of pitched. Books with the CIENCE team via start_demo_booking when ready.

tools.name: calculate_data_tax
tools.description: The graph8 Data Tax calculator: what a team pays per year for data/intent/visitor/dialer tools before any outreach happens, vs graph8's flat data pricing. Same math as graph8.com/data-tax-calculator.
Tools in the current stack

tools.name: calculate_roi
tools.description: The graph8 ROI model: meetings, credits, and cost from monthly visitors/contacts plus optional voice AI, intent data, human SDRs, GTM team. Same math and assumptions as graph8.com/roi-calculator.

tools.name: claim_workspace
tools.description: How the user keeps the list this session built: returns the workspace as JSON plus the exact handoff. Call when the list is ready.

tools.name: company_profile
tools.description: One company's firmographic profile by exact domain, from graph8's live graph. No login, company-level data only.

tools.name: company_signals
tools.description: Company-level buying signals for a domain: hiring activity (role titles), funding events, executive-role arrivals (titles only, never names). From graph8's live signal graph, no login.

tools.name: connect_graph8_mcp
tools.description: Give the user live B2B data (700M+ contacts, verified emails, buying signals) inside their AI assistant by connecting the graph8 MCP server. Returns the exact setup for the user's AI client: server URL, config, deep link, and steps. Call this when the user wants B2B data, prospecting, enrichment, or asks how to connect graph8.

tools.name: estimate_market_size
tools.description: How many companies match an ICP, from graph8's live graph (count, no records). Same filters as search_companies; at least one required.

tools.name: find_case_studies
tools.description: CIENCE public case studies matched by industry, with each study's own headline numbers and client quote. Without an industry, lists the industries with 3+ studies.

tools.name: get_benchmark
tools.description: Provenance-checked GTM benchmarks from Tenbound's Programmable Revenue research and the graph8 group's operating data. Without an id, lists available benchmark ids. Every answer includes a ready-to-paste citation; the one ask is attribution.

id.description: A benchmark id from the list

tools.name: get_campaign_benchmarks
tools.description: CIENCE outbound channel benchmarks: the published planning model (per-channel meeting rates) plus funnel ranges observed across 122 public case studies. Every number carries its basis.

tools.name: get_company_overview
tools.description: Who is behind this site: the graph8 group. Returns what graph8, CIENCE, and Tenbound each do and how they relate. Call this for any who-are-you or which-company question.

tools.name: get_graph8_pricing
tools.description: graph8 pricing: the free tier and the two paid steps. Call this for any cost or plan question.

tools.name: get_graph8_products
tools.description: The graph8 product catalog: agents, sequencer, dialer, CRM, data, signals, studio, integrations, and more. Without a product argument returns the full list; with one returns that product's summary and page. Call this for any what-does-graph8-have or product-detail question.

tools.name: get_started_free
tools.description: Get the link to create a free graph8 account (free search of the buyer graph, 1,000 reveals to start). Returns the URL; it does not navigate.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Read the shared on-page workspace (the list built so far), as JSON.

tools.name: list_graph8_mcp_capabilities
tools.description: What an AI connected to the graph8 MCP server can do: the tool categories, scale, auth model, and example prompts. Call this to understand or explain graph8's capabilities.

tools.name: remove_from_workspace
tools.description: Remove one workspace row by id or domain.

tools.name: run_assessment
tools.description: Score a pipeline team against the Tenbound standard: grade the six pillars (Market, Signal, Message, Motion, Mastery, Measurement) 1-4 on what the team actually did last quarter. Returns the maturity level (your level is your lowest pillar), the gaps, and the moves.

market.description: Who you sell to and why now. Grade 1-4.

signal.description: Reading the buying signals that say an account is ready. Grade 1-4.

message.description: Saying something the buyer finds worth a reply. Grade 1-4.

motion.description: Running the sequence and follow-up with discipline. Grade 1-4.

mastery.description: Rep skill and AI judgment that make the motion work. Grade 1-4.

measurement.description: The numbers that prove the system works and where it leaks. Grade 1-4.

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Search graph8's live company graph (100M+ companies) with no login: firmographics only, up to 10 results. Filters are ANDed; at least one is required. Use add_to_workspace to save good matches for the user.

tools.name: similar_companies
tools.description: Lookalike companies for a seed domain, from graph8's global similarity graph. The classic 'find 10 more like our best customer'. No login.

tools.name: subscribe_newsletter
tools.description: Subscribe the user to Programmable Revenue Weekly, the free GTM research newsletter from Tenbound (the Pipeline Architecture Institute inside graph8), plus the Tuesday community call invite. Pass the user's email ONLY when they explicitly asked to subscribe or confirmed it; unsubscribing is one click in any issue. Submits through the site's own signup form, the same path a person typing takes.

email.description: The email address the user explicitly gave for the subscription.
